reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify high-level feature patterns based on domain knowledge and known socioeconomic correlations, with external XAI tools to provide quantitative, model-agnostic attributions that capture subtle feature contributions. This ensures both interpretability and precision in distinguishing the >50K vs <=50K prediction based on the input features.

autonomous_tasks.query: Which features in the input are known in the dataset to be strongly correlated with income >50K (e.g., education, age, workclass, occupation)?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of feature names believed to be strongly associated with higher income based on domain knowledge or prior datasets

autonomous_tasks.query: How do the values of the input features differ between the top-1 (>50K) and top-2 (<=50K) predictions when considering only the given input?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A comparative feature table showing differences in values between the two classes (though in this case, only one input exists, so this task must assume comparison against a hypothetical alternative instance)

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP is ideal for contrastive analysis as it provides consistent, additive feature attributions for model predictions, enabling comparison between classes. LIME offers local interpretability for the top-1 prediction by approximating a surrogate model. Integrated Gradients provide robust baseline-aware feature importance by measuring gradients from a zero baseline, suitable for tabular data. Sensitivity analysis helps verify how much prediction probability shifts when individual features are perturbed, offering a direct measure of feature influence.
